scope: Regional-crop guide-only inspection, native output pending

descriptions.r02_c01: Most of the crop is existing pale cream square paving in perspective, with wide slate-gray tree canopy shadows across the upper half and narrow beveled grout lines. Exactly two loose pink fallen petal shapes are visible near the upper right; these remain flat loose petals. A small curved gray stone planter edge and clipped green leaves enter only at the top right, and tiny round-leaf tips enter at the bottom edge. Keep the route open and preserve the floor seam endpoints.
descriptions.r02_c02: The existing curved gray stone planter rim crosses from upper left toward lower right, making one soft inward bend near the center. Inside it are dense rounded green leaves, brown soil, a small clipped section of the dark trunk at upper right and a cluster of large pink blossoms on the right. A few existing fallen pink petals lie on the planter rim and paving. The lower left is cream square paving with soft canopy shadows; the lower right is the cropped edge of the existing willow canopy. The low rim remains plain gray stone, with identical footprint and height.
descriptions.r02_c03: A close crop of the existing dark brown flowering-tree trunk and large pink blossoms above rounded green shrubs occupies the top and left. Existing bright yellow-green long willow leaf clusters fill the lower half. A cream-gray stone balustrade wall angles upward along the right, including the existing square capped post, with a narrow turquoise river strip at the extreme right. Preserve each clipped object and do not complete it into another tree or post.
descriptions.r02_c04: The existing cream-gray stone riverside balustrade fills the upper half, with one tall square post near the right of center and clipped stone posts at the left. A dark gray masonry retaining wall is behind it and under the rail, with subtle block seams. Turquoise blue river water covers the lower half and meets the existing post bases. Green shrubs and tiny clipped pink blossoms occupy the top edge; the existing yellow-green willow canopy enters only at lower left. Preserve sparse broad water reflection shapes consistent with native southern water and do not add dense bright caustic threads or extra stone structures.
